A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Online Decision-Focused Learning by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic online knapsack experiments measuring decision cost and prediction error, plus a model-misspecification analysis in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original four-method knapsack comparisons in Section 4 and retains the model-misspecification results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The formal DF-OGD oracle target changes from the conditional expected surrogate in v1 H3 to the current realized surrogate in v2 Algorithm 2. Regularization, random interpolation and projected updates remain. DF-FTPL already appeared in v1 Algorithm 3; its promotion to the main text is not a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The five-item, ten-feature synthetic selection task and misspecification sweep remain. However, the reported temporal environment changes: v1 generates the latent parameter autoregressively from its preceding value, whereas v2 uses Gaussian perturbations around a fixed parameter. No new application domain or real dataset is evaluated.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands from DF-OGD versus PF-OGD to include online SPO and DF-FTPL in v2 Figure 1. DF-FTPL was previously proposed but not experimentally compared. Adding a competing decision-focused baseline substantially broadens the empirical comparison.

E3.justification: The main experiment's reported horizon increases from 2,000 to 5,000 steps, and PF-OGD's stated learning rate changes from 0.01 to 10. The replacement prediction-error panel is explicitly labeled smoothed. These revise settings and presentation of measurements within the retained synthetic task.

E4.justification: The realizability-to-misspecification analysis is retained from v1 Appendix C in v2 Appendix E, with the same interpolation experiment, 50 runs, 1,000-step horizon and identical Figure 3. No additional ablation, robustness test or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: The main experiment's reported run count decreases from 70 to 10. Both versions retain 95% Gaussian confidence intervals based on the CLT, while the misspecification experiment remains averaged over 50 runs.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the main cost and prediction-error curves and adds results for DF-FTPL and online SPO. At the end of v2 Figure 1, decision costs rank DF-FTPL, DF-OGD, online SPO, then PF-OGD, from lowest to highest. The retained methods also have changed curves, but revised experimental conditions prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains over v1. Figure 3 is unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds a general-polytope DF-FTPL static-regret theorem and a Gaussian example proving H2 in Appendix A. It revises the static-regret and oracle formulations, explicitly fixes chi to zero, and changes the reported general-polytope dynamic bound's dependence on the number of faces from n to sqrt(n). Conversely, v1 Appendix D's stronger H4 assumption, realized-loss regret guarantee and associated proofs are removed.

C1.justification: The central claim of extending DFL to online learning remains. v2 foregrounds the already-present DF-FTPL/static-regret contribution alongside DF-OGD and expands the empirical superiority claim from prediction-focused learning to online SPO as well. Its introduction additionally claims superiority in both static and dynamic environments.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting approximate oracles to SGD convergence and saddle avoidance, and attributes slower regret rates relative to prior methods to the additional smoothing trade-off. It removes v1's explicit n >= d caveat and discussion of relaxing the monotonic-path assumption. The empirical interpretation concerning misspecification remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds online SPO pseudocode and its stated surrogate loss, and revises hyperparameter and tuning disclosures. The correlated-feature construction and warm-started oracle using 10 SGD steps at learning rate 0.01 remain documented. Complete experimental tuning details for the newly evaluated DF-FTPL and SPO are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds SGD convergence and saddle-avoidance literature in Appendix B, plus explicit comparisons with prior static and dynamic regret bounds, including Zhang–Lu–Zhou and Huang–Wang. Several optimism and application references disappear. The central positioning relative to batch DFL and online bilevel optimization remains.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially reorganized around separate DF-FTPL and DF-OGD subsections with their guarantees. DF-FTPL moves into the main text, while the simplex treatment moves to Appendix C. Framework and oracle explanations are rewritten and expanded; the online-learning primer and NeurIPS checklist are removed.

P2.justification: Typography, title block, section styling and page layout change throughout. The main performance figure is redrawn with four methods, revised axes and legends, and a longer time range. The motivating figure and PF-OGD pseudocode move to the appendix, while DF-FTPL pseudocode moves into the main text. The misspecification figure itself is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the oracle target more operational, adds general-polytope analysis and broadens the reported comparison. However, new Theorem 1 specifies alpha proportional to n^1/2, which does not yield its claimed sqrt(n) dependence from the displayed bound. Algorithm 4's new SPO loss can be discontinuous when the argmin changes, conflicting with Section 4's description of a differentiable, convex surrogate. These issues affect the added theoretical and comparative evidence, leaving the net quality effect uncertain despite the clearer organization.
